The wide workshop gate stood clear ahead of them. Beyond it, strengthening rain swept past the open sides of the covered yard, driven slantwise by the wind.

Mert looked across the top edge of the mosaic panel. “Ready?”

Aya kept her side level. “Ready.”

They began with one careful step. Aya felt the urge to hurry through before the weather grew worse, but she held herself back and waited for Mert’s next movement.

Aya and Mert carried the same restored mosaic panel together through the wide workshop gate into the covered yard, maintaining their shared hold for the entire crossing. Neither released a side. The fragile panel remained intact and steady between them.

Under the cover, the rain sounded louder. Mert continued at a measured pace while keeping his side level.

Aya started half a step faster, and the panel’s edge shifted slightly toward him. She stopped pushing ahead. Aya shortened her next step and matched Mert’s pace in their shared panel carry.

Mert looked across the restored surface and observed Aya matching his pace. His shoulders eased, although his hold remained firm.

“That’s better,” he said.

Aya resisted the sharp reply that came first. He was right. When their steps stayed even, the panel stayed steadier.

“Same pace,” she said.

“Same pace,” Mert agreed.

They continued supporting the intact panel in the covered yard. The wind pressed strengthening rain beyond the shelter, but Aya no longer tried to lead Mert forward. She watched his steps, kept time with him, and held her side level.
